---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Worked letters."
description: "Front matter for an English letter, a French one, and one with a letterhead and a signature."
---

This site is HTML, and the format produces PDF, so these are the front matter blocks rather than rendered pages.
A rendered letter is attached to each [release](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-letter/releases).

## A plain letter

```yaml
---
author:
  - name: John Doe
    affiliation:
      - name: Dummy org
        department: Cool Dep
        address: Somewhere
        city: Magic city
        country: best one
        postal-code: 9999
format:
  letter-pdf:
    address:
      - Director Doe & Co
      - 35 Anthony Road
      - Newport
      - Ipswich IP3 5RT
    subject: collaboration
    opening: "Dear Sir or Madam,"
    closing: "Yours Faithfully,"
---

The body of the letter.
```

`address` is the only required option.
The author block is Quarto's own, and supplies the sender.

## Carbon copies, enclosures, and a postscript

```yaml
format:
  letter-pdf:
    cc:
      - Recipient 1
      - Recipient 2
    encl:
      - Enclosure 1
      - Enclosure 2
    ps: |
      PS: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, *consectetur* adipiscing elit.
```

Each is omitted from the letter when it is not given.

## A French letter

```yaml
format:
  letter-pdf:
    subject-title: Objet
    subject-suffix: "&nbsp;:"
```

French typography puts a non-breaking space before the colon, which is what the suffix is for.
The `meta-fr` snippet writes this block for you.

## A letterhead and a signature

```yaml
format:
  letter-pdf:
    header-image: letterhead.png
    header-image-width: "0.5\\textwidth"
    signature-image: signature.png
    signature-image-width: 4cm
```

The letterhead sits above the opening salutation, the signature between the closing and the printed name.

::: {.callout-important}
The backslash is doubled because the string is double-quoted in YAML.
Written as `"0.5\textwidth"` the backslash is consumed and the width is lost.
:::

The `meta-sig` snippet writes this block.
